bootstrapped-indian-founders-building-wi.core: Posted in last 7 days Bootstrapped Indian Founders - Building Without Venture Capital On Beyond Funded Startups, my co-host Yaduraj Joshi and I sit down with Indian businesses built without venture capital — SMEs, family businesses and bootstrapped founders who built something real the hard way. No funding stories. No valuations. Just practical lessons from someone building quietly, far from the spotlight. On Episode 4, Anju Kalhan takes us inside Bliss By Anju — a clean label snacking brand she built out of reversing her own 30-year health condition, then grew by doing the one thing most founders never dare to: she made her product smaller. No oil, no ghee, no preservatives. A few things that stuck with us: → In a crowded market, what you remove can set you apart faster than what you add. → You're not selling the product. You're selling trust — and no discount buys what a sample in the hand can. → Every sales channel has one job. Marketplaces make you seen; your own website makes you money. Don't confuse the two. Listen on Spotify: https://lnkd.in/gZnAKtBU If you're running a business without funding, or know someone who is, I'd love to hear from you. We're always lining up our next guests. Beyond Funded Startups

k12-deaf-and-hard-of-hearing-students-mi.author: R. H. Odland
k12-deaf-and-hard-of-hearing-students-mi.core: Posted in last 7 days K-12 Deaf & Hard of Hearing Students - Missing IEP Services When I was a kid at the Atlanta Area School for the Deaf, I didn't have words for it yet, but I could already see the gap between what a school promised Deaf kids and what we got. Decades later, that gap is still there. Now it shows up in data. Through the National Deaf Education Data Index (NDEDI), I've been going state by state through what's reported about Deaf and hard of hearing students. The numbers tell part of the story. Families, interpreters and teachers know the rest. So I'm asking. If a Deaf or hard of hearing student in K-12 is going without services their IEP says they get, I want to hear about it. That could be an interpreter who never shows up, or one who isn't qualified. It could be captions or AI tools standing in for real access, or a placement that quietly changed without anyone asking the family. I also want to hear when money is involved: funding meant for Deaf education that went somewhere else, contracts that don't add up, or budgets that no one will explain. Email [email redacted]. I read every one and I follow up. Names stay out of anything I publish unless you tell me otherwise. You don't need proof in hand. Tell me what you're seeing, and I'll do the digging. #DeafEducation #IEP #NDEDI #Accessibility #SpecialEducation

palo-alto-networks-employees-acquisition.author: Niels Hoekman
palo-alto-networks-employees-acquisition.core: Posted in last 7 days Palo Alto Networks Employees - Acquisition Culture & Power Abuse Since sharing my experiences with Palo Alto Networks, I've received a significant number of private messages, particularly from people connected to the CyberArk acquisition. And the stories deserve to be heard. I'm collecting these experiences and will be starting a LinkedIn series covering different aspects of what people have experienced inside Palo Alto Networks, including: - Power abuse: leadership behaviour, intimidation and toxic workplace cultures. - How women are treated: inequality, disrespect and inappropriate behaviour. - Life after an acquisition: what really happens to employees, teams and company cultures once the acquisition is complete. - Speaking up: what happens when employees raise concerns and expect HR to protect them. And this conversation shouldn't stop at Palo Alto Networks. With acquisitions and industry consolidation involving companies like CrowdStrike and Zscaler, these are conversations worth having across the entire industry. If you've experienced something similar, I want to hear your story. You can reach out to me via DM. I will treat every message with care, respect and confidentiality. I will not publish names or identifying details without consent. It's time we talked about the human side of acquisitions, leadership and corporate culture. Because behind every acquisition are real people. And they deserve better. Follow me and hit the 🔔 on my profile. This is going to be a series, and this is only the beginning.
